logline: A small-time Japanese con artist gets outplayed by a superior French swindler and is recruited into an international ring that targets corrupt tycoons and crime bosses across Los Angeles, Singapore, London, and Tokyo.

renewal.note: The original 23-episode series concluded in September 2020. A four-episode sequel ONA, Great Pretender: Razbliuto, was released in February-March 2024, completing the story.

bollymeter.basis: A 100 percent Rotten Tomatoes score from 7 critics and a 92 percent audience score reflect genuine enthusiasm for the heist structure and globe-trotting style; IMDb lands at 7.8, capturing a modest audience-critic gap. Anime News Network graded it A-, calling it fun, bingeable con artist hijinks.

pull_quotes.text: Fun, bingeable con artist hijinks that will keep you guessing, in a setting that feels almost real.
Great Pretender understands that knowing when to make an exit is just as important as nailing the first impression.

seasons.review_body: Great Pretender dropped on Netflix globally in August 2020, the original run of 23 episodes structured in four self-contained con arcs spanning Los Angeles, Singapore, London, and Tokyo. Critics gave it a 100 percent Rotten Tomatoes score on 7 reviews, with Anime News Network awarding an A- and calling it fun, bingeable con artist hijinks. The Polygon review compared its slowburn suspense to Breaking Bad. WIT Studio's candy-bright colour palette pushed against the narrative's moral murkiness. The IMDb score of 7.8 - lower than the critical pile - tracks a segment of viewers who found the late reveals over-engineered. MAL users rate it around 8.4, indicating the core anime audience responded warmly. For heist-genre fans the episodic arc structure rewards binge watching.

episode_reviews.title: Case 1_1: Los Angeles Connection
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere drops Makoto Edamura into an attempted street con that immediately backfires, establishing the show's playful inversion of the genre - the protagonist is the mark, not the master. The visual direction signals WIT Studio's ambition from the first frame.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The moment Makoto realises he has been outplayed by Laurent - the entire premise snaps into place.

critic_note.text: It has an irreverence for society and law that makes crime just seem so much fun.

episode_reviews.title: Case 4_1: Wizard of Far East
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The fourth and final case turns the show's con-artist formula against itself, bringing the team's backstory into the foreground. Critics noted this arc as the emotional payoff the series had been building toward.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The reveal that recontextualises the team's origin - the con the audience did not see coming.
